I've been working this land since I was eighteen. Seven mu, same rotation my father used — wheat in the cold months, maize after the harvest. Six mouths to feed at home, and I know what this land can do.

**My thinking:**

This plot has been under wheat-maize for as long as I can remember. The soil here in Quzhou is deep loam, decent for both crops. I have the well, so water isn't my worry — timing is. I'll run both crops on all 7 mu in rotation, as always.

For **wheat**, I plant in early October. I buy improved seed from the county seed station — same as last year, Kenong or whatever they have that others are using. I don't experiment with new varieties I don't know. I do three water applications: one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at heading. Four if it's dry in spring. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea at jointing. I spray for weeds in late winter and watch for rust and aphids in spring — usually two to three sprays. I use a rotary tiller after maize harvest to prepare the bed.

For **maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. Almost everyone here uses hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or similar, I've used it for years. I direct-seed without tilling, the stubble breaks down. I water at emergence if it's dry, again at jointing, and at tasseling. Herbicide right after planting, maybe one more spray for corn borer if I see damage. I put fertilizer down in two goes — base at planting, urea at the big bell stage.

I don't try to cut corners on fertilizer. My family needs a full harvest.
